q1_assessment.gating_risk: empirical axis, not infrastructure (infrastructure and theory are already Tier-1 grade)
q1_assessment.why: After GAP-45/54/56/57 the picture is sharper and harsher. (a) The namesake mechanism is null: on R1 at NFE=150 the memory term ties a no-memory restart in 3/3 seeds, and beta=0 collapses the arm outright, so no current result can be attributed to the blend. (b) R5c's historical -28.43% was the smoke checkpoint; at matched NFE the production cell regresses +9.52% on 3 draws, and only the under-trained w16e1_5k wins (-9.37%, 3/3 draws) - a model-conditional cell. (c) The positive cells are now R6 (3 seeds, N=3000, scPerplexity d_z=-0.84), R5c-boundary (3 draws, N=1000, model-conditional) and R1 (N=1000 but ONE seed). (d) K7 shows the framework is 12.6x less novel and that has never been measured on the same samples as R1's +74% validity, so the two headline results currently read as contradictory.
q1_assessment.decisive_missing_piece: One 3-seed positive at N=1000 on a canonical checkpoint (GAP-59: R1 seeds 43/44), plus one measurement that puts validity and novelty on the same axis (GAP-60) so R1 and K7 are one trade-off rather than two stories, plus a yes/no on whether the memory term earns anything anywhere (GAP-61).
q1_assessment.if_met: Q1-defensible: theory + byte-stable infrastructure + a 3-seed N=1000 positive cell + an explicit validity/novelty trade-off + honest negatives (R5c production, R5b, K7) + a compute ledger. The mechanism claim must be restated either way: the perturbation channel is what the evidence supports.
q1_assessment.if_not_met: Still submittable as a framework / operating-regime paper at TNNLS/TCyb/Information Fusion, but 'steady accept' is not supportable; fall back to KBS/EAAI rather than forcing a SOTA framing.

blocking_point.name: evidence homogeneity: one 3-seed N=1000 positive, and a mechanism that the evidence supports
blocking_point.detail: R1 (the strongest cross-domain positive) is single-seed at N=1000; R3 is single-seed and below the Bonferroni floor; R2 is single-seed with d=-0.099; R5b's effect size is an N=200 FID number that the project's own calibration says is inflated 40-65%; K7's novelty inversion has never been put on the same axis as R1's validity gain; and the memory blend - the paper's namesake - is null wherever it has been tested.

mechanism_update_2026_10_21.finding: The restart blend m*x1+(1-m)*x0 is a variance-shrinkage operator, not a sampler-accuracy operator. It contracts the sample cloud toward the model's conditional mean.
mechanism_update_2026_10_21.evidence: rho_base = tr(S_gen)/tr(S_ref) in the FID projection space predicts the sign of the measured FID delta in 4/4 MNIST-FM checkpoints (production 0.782 / w16e1_10k 0.752 / w16e1_60k 0.704 -> FID up; w16e1_5k 1.006 -> FID down -9.65%). docs/audit/gap64-r5c-operating-regime.md
mechanism_update_2026_10_21.what_it_unifies: K7 novelty -42.9 pp (shrinkage removes tail samples), R1 +74% hmmscan hits and R6 scPerplexity d_z=-0.84 (both reward a smoother, higher-likelihood population), and the R5c split (helps only the one checkpoint whose base dispersion is at or above the data).
mechanism_update_2026_10_21.what_it_forbids: 'For any FM model the framework improves inference quality' is FALSE on fidelity metrics and cannot be made true by better wiring: the operator is one-directional. The framework's own NFE allocator was wired in and measured (GAP-64): no sign flip.
mechanism_update_2026_10_21.what_replaces_it: A never-worse selector: measure rho_base on a ~200-sample pilot, apply the framework iff rho_base >= 1. GAP-65 tests the rule out of family (R5b/R1/R3) with a pre-registered 6-of-7 threshold.

open_gaps.est_wall: ~3 h (pilot batches only; no new N=1000 sampling)
open_gaps.gap: GAP-64 established that the restart blend is a variance-shrinkage operator and that the sign of the R5c delta is predicted 4/4 by rho_base = tr(S_gen)/tr(S_ref) in the FID projection (shrinkage pays iff rho_base >= 1). That is a hypothesis fitted on four checkpoints of ONE model family. Until it is tested out of family, the paper cannot claim a universal statement, and the current claim ('the framework improves any FM model') is false on fidelity metrics because the operator is one-directional. The deployable form is a selector: measure rho on a ~200-sample pilot, apply the framework only when rho_base >= 1. With that rule the honest universal statement is 'never worse than the base sampler, strictly better when the base is over-dispersed'.
